Construct a disposable mutation at the actual production `count_calls` occurrence-status case, after `matches` has captured the failed producer's complete output and before it is discarded by the error return. A sufficient one-line mutation is that case's `0|1) ;;` to `0|1|9) ;;`. Confine it to the production count_calls function and its occurrence case, not embedded mutation text or candidate discovery. In this test only the selected fourth operation emits status 9; earlier real operations are unaffected. No phase state, test hook or changed status handling belongs in the production checker itself.

This mutation leaves `matches` unchanged and lets the existing, unmodified `wc -l`/normalization derive the numeric count from those occurrences. The registered caller's error check, per-file comparison, marker check, aggregate and tree recount all remain intact. Do not use `actual="$count"`, a literal count fallback, a registry-derived value, an empty-output replacement, a caller status edit, or a second compensating mutation.

Verify the actual disposable diff, not construction labels or checksum change alone: exactly the intended production occurrence-status line changes at that function/case, with one hunk and no other changed lines. Context must establish the actual function/case; a one-hunk count alone is insufficient. Keep the disposable diff or concise exact diff in the test evidence.

Record and check the selected producer's real occurrence payload and the numeric result produced by the existing count command on the mutant run. Minimal temporary shim evidence is sufficient: retain the delegated selected rg stdout and the delegated registered-phase wc result without mixing this evidence into checker data. The expected count is an assertion about observed output, never a value supplied to the checker. This is bounded evidence for the existing test, not a tracing subsystem. The unchanged production data path plus the exact mutation diff must show how those occurrences become the registered count.
